title: Short Stuff: Rescuing Mistreated Pets
summary: Short Stuff installment on what to do when you see a mistreated or endangered animal, such as a dog left in a hot car or neglected in a yard. The hosts explain that breaking into a car or house to rescue an animal can bring trespassing or theft charges, though about 14 states give civil immunity for breaking a car window to free an animal in immediate danger, with conditions such as trying to find the owner, checking whether the door is unlocked, using minimal force, and calling 911 and waiting for authorities. They discuss how animal cruelty enforcement varies, including animal control agencies, humane societies with deputized officers, and police training gaps. They then cover reporting non-emergency neglect online, keeping a log of dates and times, the option of anonymous tips, and requesting a Humane Society wellness check. Chuck closes with a personal story of a neighborhood rescue of an emaciated dog left in a backyard, and the hosts stress that the rescue was instinctive and not advice to copy.
topics: breaking car window to save pet

segments.title: Welcome and overview
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the topic: what to do about a mistreated animal you see on property you own or visit, and why you should not break in to rescue it.

segments.title: Breaking into cars to rescue animals
segments.summary: The hosts explain the legal risks of entering property to free an animal, noting trespassing or theft charges. About 14 states offer civil immunity for breaking a car window to free an animal in immediate danger, with conditions: believe the animal is in immediate danger, look for the owner, check whether the door is unlocked, use minimal force, and call 911. Indiana still requires paying half the vehicle damage. Local laws may differ, as in Boise, Idaho.
topics: breaking car window to save pet

segments.title: Police training on animal cruelty
segments.summary: Chuck notes that calling 911 may route the case to animal control. He cites an ASPCA finding that under 20 percent of police received such training in 2010 and fewer than half knew the laws. Josh cites a 2015 supplemental survey where half of officers encountered dog fighting and many wanted more training.

segments.title: Who enforces animal cruelty laws
segments.summary: For animals in distress without immediate danger, the hosts explain that 911 dispatch may send police or animal control. Enforcement is handled by a city or county division, and in some places by a charitable organization.

segments.title: Humane Society deputized officers
segments.summary: Chuck says that in 34 states the Humane Society has deputized animal control officers who act as police for animal cruelty. Josh makes a joke claiming armed officers in some states, which Chuck says he fell for; Josh clarifies it was a joke.

segments.title: Off-topic movie chat
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the movies Long Legs and Black Coat's Daughter and mention watching Blowout.

segments.title: Reporting neglect online and complaints
segments.summary: Chuck advises finding local animal control agencies and their websites to file complaints, even for a dog chained outside that is not dying. Complaints can be filed online.

segments.title: Documenting neglect and anonymous tips
segments.summary: The hosts advise giving detailed reasons, the correct address, and dates and times of abuse, keeping a log. Anonymous tips may be possible, but reporters may be called to testify as witnesses.

segments.title: Humane Society wellness checks
segments.summary: Josh describes requesting a wellness check from the Humane Society when someone suspects neglect without immediate danger; an officer investigates and the caller may receive a Hero ribbon.

segments.title: Chuck's rescue story
segments.summary: Chuck tells how, through a local rescue network, he and a friend cut a chain-link fence to rescue an emaciated dog left in a backyard after a family moved. The dog later lived a long, happy life and died a few months before Chuck checked in. Chuck posted a tribute on Instagram. The hosts say the rescue was instinctive and not advice to follow.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck wrap up, urging listeners to watch for animals in need and noting the show's production credit.
